items.title: Avoidance of Infinite Loops in Repetitive Actions
items.description: Do not perform the exact same action multiple times consecutively within a single trajectory unless necessary.
items.content: The agent failed because it repeatedly executed the identical click command without changing parameters or strategy, triggering a stuck detector and preventing task progression. Future tasks should vary actions dynamically based on context rather than repeating the same input sequentially to avoid infinite loops.

items.title: Prioritization of Explicit Search Interfaces Over Navigation History
items.description: Do not assume that clicking previous navigation items will lead to specific search results pages, even if they appear to have similar functions.
items.content: The agent spent steps navigating through historical links (like "history") instead of finding the primary interface for initiating a new search query. Successful task resolution requires identifying and using the explicit search entry point (such as a search bar or home page) rather than relying on indirect navigation paths.

items.title: Immediate Intervention When Progress Stalls Due to Repetition
items.description: Implement a fallback mechanism that forces a state change when an action results in no visible progress after a few attempts.
items.content: The agent failed because it continued repeating the same command despite likely exhausting available options in that specific context. A robust strategy requires monitoring for stagnation (e.g., repeated identical actions) and automatically switching to alternative approaches, such as restarting navigation or selecting different menu items, rather than persisting on a single ineffective path.

items.title: Scroll once to surface the Sponsored vs Organic split
items.description: A single scroll past the first results reveals the sponsored-versus-organic boundary that aids disambiguation.
items.content: When the desired item is not on the first results page, scrolling once is usually enough to surface a Sponsored vs Organic split that helps disambiguation between paid placement and ranked organic matches.

items.title: Handling Search Result Pages as Landing Pages
items.description: The agent successfully navigates a site that redirects to search results instead of an intermediate product detail page.
items.content: When targeting specific products on e-commerce platforms, it is critical to first identify whether the landing page is already populated with search results; attempting to fill input fields directly on such pages may result in errors if the browser does not detect the active input element without scrolling.

items.title: Prioritize Scroll Actions Over Immediate Input Attempts
items.description: When navigating to a search results page where query inputs are unavailable or obscured, scrolling is more effective than immediate text entry actions.
items.content: The trajectory demonstrates that successful navigation often requires manual scrolling to reveal hidden elements like the search bar before attempting to type into it, rather than assuming input fields are immediately accessible upon page load.

items.title: Robustness in Handling Repeated Parse Failures
items.description: The agent persists with a plan even after encountering multiple consecutive failures, indicating a need for robust error handling and retry mechanisms.
items.content: A successful trajectory implies that the system must remain stable despite repeated parse failures when executing automated inputs, requiring fallback strategies like scrolling or waiting for page states to stabilize before retrying input actions.

items.title: Robustness Against Search Query Syntax Variations
items.description: The agent successfully navigated a target page but failed when attempting to simulate typing search terms with incorrect action syntax, resulting in repeated failures and an eventual time-out.
items.content: This trajectory highlights that the system relies heavily on correct action formatting; even successful navigation to the goal page does not guarantee success if subsequent user actions (like typing) are malformed or unsupported by the parsing engine. Future tasks should ensure search queries are executed with valid syntax before proceeding.

items.title: Mitigation Strategies for Infinite Scrolling Loops
items.description: The agent encountered a stuck state where it repeated an invalid action five times, triggering a stuck-detector timeout that aborted the run prematurely.
items.content: Repeated scrolling or clicking without interaction yielded diminishing results and eventually triggered a safety mechanism to stop the process. Successful agents should implement loops with strict iteration limits (e.g., 3-5 attempts) and incorporate fallback strategies like switching actions or retrying previous steps upon detecting redundancy.

items.title: Separation of Navigation and Interaction States
items.description: The agent reached the search results page but failed to retrieve relevant items due to an inability to parse and execute specific typing commands, leading to a timeout.
items.content: Success depends not only on reaching the correct destination but also on executing valid user interactions within that context; if an interaction fails immediately upon entry or persists after navigation, it may indicate a fundamental limitation in the system's capability for that specific task type rather than a lack of effort.

items.title: Use of Interactive Elements for Navigation
items.description: The task was completed by clicking a specific interactive element to proceed through the search results.
items.content: Successful navigation often requires identifying and interacting with the correct button or link that links to the desired profile or result, rather than relying on static text or scrolling alone.

items.title: Avoidance of Ambiguous Action Commands
items.description: The agent failed when attempting to use a generic 'stop' action without providing explicit navigation parameters.
items.content: When an interface allows direct control over elements (like buttons), abstract commands such as "move down" or "go next" are insufficient; precise targeting of interactive components is necessary for success.

items.title: Importance of Action-Response Feedback Loops
items.description: The trajectory demonstrates that repeated 'stop' commands triggered a stuck-detector due to lack of progress detection.
items.content: Effective task execution requires monitoring the agent's state after each action; if an action does not result in reaching the next stage (like entering a new page), subsequent actions should be adjusted or retried with different parameters.

items.title: Avoid Clicking Intersected Overlay Elements
items.description: When attempting to interact with a primary navigation element, always verify that no overlapping modal overlays or floating menus are intercepting pointer events before executing the action.
items.content: The trajectory failed because an overlay div was blocking interactions with the intended navigation button; future attempts should prioritize closing or dismissing any visible popovers and modals before proceeding to interact with underlying menu items.

items.title: Use Explicit Element Selection When Interacting With Dynamic Navigation Components
items.description: For dynamic UI components like hamburger menus where IDs or ARIA references may be stale or unreliable, use explicit selectors that include the element's specific attributes (e.g., role="button") rather than relying solely on generic index-based click commands.
items.content: Since the agent used a generic index reference for a non-interactive anchor tag which often behaves differently than expected, future attempts should target elements by their unique functional roles and specific DOM attributes to ensure correct selection of interactive controls like navigation toggles.

items.title: Prioritize Sorting Before Filtering On Large Product Lists
items.description: When navigating to product search results pages containing extensive listings with multiple sort options and filters, perform sorting actions directly on the page's primary interaction elements rather than relying on implicit filtering via URL parameters or modal selectors.
items.content: The agent attempted to apply a sort filter through an unconfirmed menu mechanism which resulted in a deadlock; future strategies should execute the primary action (sorting) immediately on the visible list item or search bar controls instead of attempting to configure filters via secondary menus that may be unstable or irrelevant for basic sorting tasks.

items.title: Preventing Infinite Loop in Tool Failure Scenarios
items.description: Ensure the system does not repeatedly retry failed tool execution steps until a specific duration threshold or logical safety condition is met.
items.content: The trajectory failed due to an infinite loop where the same erroneous action was executed multiple times without interruption. Future agents must implement a mechanism to detect repeated failures and immediately trigger a safety abort or switch to alternative strategies rather than continuing to repeat the last command.

items.title: Ensuring Search Queries Match Platform-Specific Syntax Requirements
items.description: Verify that search terms for specific platforms like Amazon include necessary modifiers such as 'in site:Amazon' or platform-specific URL parameters instead of relying solely on a general query format.
items.content: Generic search queries are often insufficient when targeting specialized marketplaces; therefore, agents must dynamically adjust their input syntax to align with the platform's unique search logic (e.g., appending domain prefixes) before attempting an action.

items.title: Implementing Immediate Error Feedback for Invalid Actions
items.description: Provide explicit feedback or alerts to users immediately upon detecting a tool execution failure, rather than allowing the user to blindly retry the same incorrect command.
items.content: When an automated step fails due to syntax or context issues, the system should inform the user of the nature of the error and suggest immediate corrective actions (such as revising the search term) instead of looping indefinitely, which improves usability and prevents resource exhaustion.

items.title: Avoiding Infinite Loops on Search Input
items.description: Relying on fixed sequential attempts to type into an input field without detecting failure states is prone to getting stuck in infinite loops.
items.content: Strategies involving dynamic monitoring of the input field's state or immediate fallbacks upon parse failures should be implemented instead of blindly repeating actions until success.

items.title: Prioritizing Filtering Over Explicit Queries
items.description: Attempting to type highly specific keywords like "cheapest" into a search box is inefficient when a built-in sorting or filtering mechanism is available directly on the interface.
items.content: Users should first verify if the current page offers a sort filter (e.g., Price: Low to High) or advanced filters that can achieve the goal without requiring arbitrary text input.

items.title: Implementing Stuck-State Detection Mechanisms
items.description: Failing to detect when an action has failed multiple times in a row leads to redundant execution and eventual timeout or abort by stuck detectors.
items.content: A robust solution requires integrating logic that halts further attempts upon repeated failure within a short window, allowing the agent to switch strategies immediately rather than continuing the same path.

items.title: Avoid Modal Interactions During Navigation Tasks
items.description: Do not attempt to click or type into elements while a modal dialog is intercepting pointer events, as this causes persistent timeouts and subsequent parse failures.
items.content: When navigating to a search page, agents must wait for all overlay modals (such as floating close panels) to disappear before interacting with input fields like search boxes. Attempting actions during this interference leads to repeated timeout errors and invalid action states.

items.title: Handle Input Field Parse Failures Gracefully
items.description: When an element is identified by a generic ID but fails due to a parsing error, the agent should verify if another valid input field exists on the page instead of repeatedly retrying the failed action.
items.content: If an initial interaction with a primary input control (e.g., search textbox) results in a parse failure, it indicates the target may have been lost or obscured by UI overlays. The agent must scan for alternative active input fields and prioritize those that do not trigger errors over blindly repeating the same invalid command.

items.title: Diagnose Click Timeout Errors Caused by UI Overlays
items.description: When a click action times out, check if an inactive element or floating modal is blocking the pointer; if so, the solution requires dismissing the overlay before performing the intended click.
items.content: A common cause of click timeouts during search interactions is an invisible or non-interactive popup covering the target button. The agent should identify elements with high z-order but no click functionality (like scrollers or modals) and ensure they are closed or scrolled away before executing the next action.

items.title: Detection of Input Field Constraints Before Attempting Text Entry
items.description: Ensure the target input field supports text input operations before executing typing commands to prevent parsing failures.
items.content: Agents must verify that the current element is a valid text input field (such as a search bar or comment box) and that the action associated with it is defined as 'type' or equivalent, rather than assuming the ability to type without checking the context.

items.title: Prevention of Redundant Action Loops Using Timeout Triggers
items.description: Implement automated termination mechanisms for repetitive attempts when an action fails immediately upon execution.
items.content: If a specific action results in a consistent failure (like parsing errors) within a few consecutive steps, the system should automatically abort further iterations instead of continuing to repeat the same failed logic.

items.title: Verification of Search Query Parameters and Filters Before Searching
items.description: Confirm that required filters or parameters for the search task are properly selected before issuing the final search command.
items.content: When navigating to a specific search interface (such as an international shipping filter), it is critical to verify all necessary conditions—like category selection, sorting options, or price filters—are correctly applied and recognized by the system prior to executing the search action.

items.title: Avoid looping when searching for specific terms via input fields
items.description: Recognize that repeatedly attempting the same action after a parse failure indicates a potential mismatch between the intended search term and the expected input field context.
items.content: When an agent attempts to type a phrase into an input field but receives a parse error, it should immediately verify whether the current focus is indeed an input field rather than looping indefinitely or retrying the same action. A successful strategy involves first checking if the required element (e.g., search bar) exists and is active before proceeding with typing actions.

items.title: Ensure input parameters align with the tool's expected syntax
items.description: Prioritize validating the format and argument structure of commands before executing them to avoid runtime failures.
items.content: An agent must ensure that its selected command arguments (such as "type") match the specific requirements of the underlying tool or platform being used. If a command is known to fail due to syntax issues, attempting different variations of the same logic without adjusting the command structure will not yield results; instead, the agent should refactor the command to comply with expected parameters before execution.

items.title: Implement early termination for repetitive failed actions
items.description: Detect patterns of repeated failure and trigger an abort strategy immediately to prevent resource wastage.
items.content: When a plan fails multiple times consecutively or involves repeating the same action without resolution, the agent should invoke a stopping mechanism rather than continuing to loop through identical steps. This prevents the system from wasting computational resources and allows for immediate re-evaluation of the overall plan instead of blindly persisting on an ineffective approach.

items.title: Handling Interacting Elements with Modal Overlays
items.description: Prevent clicks from failing when a modal dialog intercepts the browser viewport and blocks pointer events for underlying controls.
items.content: The agent failed because a floating modal overlay covered the target input element, causing the click action to time out despite the element being visible and enabled. Future interactions should check for active modal overlays blocking pointer events before executing clicks on other elements, potentially by dismissing them first or selecting alternative interactive targets within the same context.

items.title: Improving Robustness of Click Actions in Dynamic Environments
items.description: Increase the reliability of click operations by handling transient states where page content is visible but unclickable due to overlay interference.
items.content: Simple visibility checks are insufficient when elements are obscured by full-screen modals; strategies should include waiting for overlays to close or implementing specific logic to bypass blocked interaction zones. Adding a fallback mechanism to handle repeated failures caused by these blocking conditions will reduce the need for aggressive retry loops and prevent agent stalling.

items.title: Redefining Strategy Limits Around Stuck Detectors
items.description: Avoid triggering stuck detector errors by recognizing when repeated attempts are futile due to environmental constraints rather than algorithmic issues.
items.content: Repeatedly attempting a single interaction that consistently fails due to modal overlays is inefficient and leads to premature termination. The agent should recognize environmental blockers as a distinct category from technical bugs and adjust its strategy immediately upon detecting consistent failure modes, opting to change tactics instead of escalating retry attempts.

items.description: Avoid executing the exact same failed action repeatedly without introducing variation or switching strategies.

items.description: Ensure that all command parameters and formatting rules are verified and correct before triggering any user interaction function.
items.content: Agents must validate their action definitions against system requirements prior to submission; failing this check results in immediate parse failure, making it crucial to prioritize syntax correction over repeated execution attempts.

items.title: Implementing Adaptive Strategy Switches Upon Failure
items.description: When a search or input action fails, dynamically alter the approach by either changing the command structure or switching to a different functional pathway rather than cycling through identical actions.
items.content: Effective navigation requires an adaptive response loop where failure triggers a strategic pivot—such as verifying arguments, selecting alternate input methods, or revising the query format—rather than a static cycle of repeating a doomed strategy.
